title: The maxExchangeRate ceiling is set at roughly twice the vault's current share price, so the protection decays into an outage as yield accrues
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.7.3.2.4.3 states its calibration explicitly: "The following ensures 1 share can represent at most 4 PYUSD (**current share price is 2**)", via `setMaxExchangeRate(STEAKHOUSE_PYUSD_MAIN, 1e18, 4e6)`. The USDC v2 vault uses the same doubling: a 2 USDC ceiling for a vault whose shares start near parity (A...7.2.2.4.3).

A multiple of the observed price is a reasonable heuristic — tight enough that a manipulation large enough to matter is caught, loose enough that ordinary accrual does not trip it. But the two quantities move differently. The ceiling is a static governance parameter; the share price of a yield-bearing vault rises monotonically. A 2x buffer is therefore a **time budget**, not a permanent margin: at the point the price doubles, deposits into that vault begin reverting.

That gives the parameter an unusual failure mode among Grove's controls. Most of them fail closed in the safe direction and stay there. This one fails closed and then *stays* closed, silently converting a risk control into an availability outage that looks identical to a misconfiguration.

It also means the ceiling must be periodically raised, and each raise is an opportunity to over-raise. The safer long-run design would express the bound relative to a recorded reference rather than as an absolute figure; as written, the protection's effectiveness depends on governance maintaining it at the right cadence for each vault's yield.

No review interval, owner, or trigger for raising it is documented anywhere in this section.
description: The PYUSD vault is capped at 4 PYUSD per share against a current price of 2; without periodic increases a yield-bearing vault eventually breaches its own ceiling and deposits start reverting.
